props.text: What patients ask before they visit.
What is a prosthodontist, and how is that different from a general dentist?

A prosthodontist is a dental specialist in replacing and rebuilding teeth: implants, full arches, dentures, crowns and veneers. Dr. Esam Nahlah is a board-certified prosthodontist, a Diplomate of the American Board of Prosthodontics, and treats patients at both offices, in McLean near Tysons Corner and in Alexandria.

Two offices in Northern Virginia. Tysons Corner: 7901 Jones Branch Drive, Suite 220, McLean, VA 22102, (703) 448-3312. Alexandria: 2855 Duke Street, Alexandria, VA 22314, new patients (571) 617-7245. Both are open Monday to Thursday, 8 am to 5 pm, and Friday, 8 am to 2 pm.
How much do dental implants cost in McLean and Alexandria?

It depends on how many implants you need, whether bone grafting is required and which teeth go on them, which is why two quotes for the same mouth can differ by thousands. The cost is set at your consultation, once Dr. Nahlah has seen your 3D scan and you have chosen an option. Call (703) 448-3312 in McLean or (571) 617-7245 in Alexandria to book.
How can I pay for treatment?
Cash, check, credit card, most PPO dental plans, or financing of up to $60,000 over terms of up to 96 months.
Do you offer sedation for anxious patients?
Yes. Nitrous oxide and oral sedation are both available, given at the office by the practice.
Can I leave with new teeth the same day?
With All-on-4, in most cases yes: you leave the same visit wearing a fixed provisional arch, and the final zirconia arch follows three to four months later.
What happens at the first visit?
An office tour, a consultation with Dr. Nahlah, digital X-rays, an examination and a cleaning.

props.text: Implant-Supported Dentures in McLean & Alexandria, VA
What patients ask about snap-in dentures.

Snap-in dentures, also called snap-on or implant-retained dentures, are implant-supported dentures: a removable denture that clips onto two or more implants instead of resting on the gums. It will not slip, loosen or fall out, and it still comes out for cleaning.
Snap-in dentures or All-on-4: which should I choose?

It comes down to whether you want teeth that come out. Implant-supported dentures are removable, give back around 60% of natural function and cost a moderate amount. A fixed full arch such as All-on-4 stays in, is fixed to four to eight implants, gives back over 98% and costs the most. Your consultation and 3D scan show which your bone and budget allow.
How many implants hold an implant-supported denture?
Two or more. A fixed full arch takes four to eight.
Do implant-supported dentures stop bone loss?
They help. The implants load the jawbone, which keeps it healthier; a traditional denture rests on the gums and does nothing to halt jawbone loss.
Will I be without teeth during treatment?

No. Treatment runs in four stages (consultation, any preparation such as extractions or bone grafting, surgery, then the final teeth), and most patients leave surgery with temporary teeth, so you can function while you heal.
How much do implant-supported dentures cost?

Their cost sits between traditional dentures and a fixed full arch. Your figure is set at the consultation, once the number of implants and any preparation are known. Financing is available: a financial coordinator helps you apply, and many patients are approved instantly.
Some. They may still need relines or repairs over the years, and you take them out to clean them. A fixed full arch needs no additional maintenance beyond the care you give natural teeth.

Why is there no price list on this page?
Because an honest one cannot exist. Two people missing the same tooth can need entirely different treatment depending on what the bone is doing. You get a real number after the scan, in writing.

Some plans offer limited coverage. The practice files claims on your behalf and works to get every benefit your plan entitles you to. Whether that is a large or small share depends entirely on the plan.
Can I finance the whole case?
In most cases yes, through CareCredit, Proceed Finance or LendingClub. Proceed Finance carries the longest terms of the three, up to 96 months.
Is a second opinion really free?
Yes, on implant surgery. If you have been quoted elsewhere, bring the plan and any imaging.
